title: Practice 6: The present for the future, and «let's go»

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Возьми обезьяну и ___ (летать — to fly, there and back or in general) с нею!
exercises.why: **летай** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **летать** (to fly) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **лететь** for one direction. imperative: лета́й · лета́йте. — Wiktionary, «летать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Летать: this verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Like the verb "ходить" (по комнате) the verb "летать" may be used to indicate motion without a definite goal. Note. — Do not confuse the following: Самолёт летает над городом. (motion without a definite goal) — Самолёт летит над городом. (motion towards a definite goal) — both: The aircraft is flying over the city.» — DLI, Lesson 55.  Compare: «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Капитан летит в Вашингтон.» · «Он иногда летает в Вашингтон.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  ·  From Александр Беляев, «Ариэль».
exercises.context: Летать: this verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation. (DLI, Lesson 22)

exercises.q: Не ___ (ездить — to go by vehicle, ride, there and back or in general) к ним.
exercises.why: **езди** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **ездить** (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **ехать** for one direction. imperative: е́зди · е́здите. — Wiktionary, «ездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The imperative of идти is идите; the imperative of ехать is поезжайте. Идите в класс! (on foot) Поезжайте в штаб! (by vehicle) The familiar forms do not have the ending -те: Иди! Поезжай!» — DLI, Lesson 28.  «The Imperative is: идите! — (не) ходите! — пойдите! For ехать: (не) ездите! — поезжайте!» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The familiar form of the imperative does not have the ending -те: войдите — войди, идите — иди, приезжайте — приезжай, приходите — приходи.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь).» — DLI, Lesson 22.  Compare: «В прошлом году я ездил в Россию.» (I went to Russia (and returned) last year.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Да, я ходил (ездил) туда утром.» (Yes, I went there in the morning.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  From Николай Островский, «Рождённые бурей».
exercises.context: The imperative of идти is идите; the imperative of ехать is поезжайте. (DLI, Lesson 28)

exercises.q: Заплочено и ___ (ездить — to go by vehicle, ride, there and back or in general).
exercises.why: **ездим** is the present tense (1st person plural) of **ездить** (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **ехать** for one direction. present: я е́зжу · ты е́здишь · он е́здит · мы е́здим · вы е́здите · они е́здят. — Wiktionary, «ездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь).» — DLI, Lesson 22.  Compare: «В прошлом году я ездил в Россию.» (I went to Russia (and returned) last year.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Да, я ходил (ездил) туда утром.» (Yes, I went there in the morning.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  From Михаил Булгаков, «Площадь на колёсах».
exercises.context: Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: ___ (побежать — to start running) куда-нибудь? — упрашивал, метаясь на месте, Висленёв.
exercises.why: **побежимте** is the imperative (вы, plural or polite) of **побежать** (to start running, to break into a run) — the perfective of **бежать**, «set out». imperative: побеги́ · побеги́те. — Wiktionary, «побежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Николай Лесков, «На ножах».
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: По вечерам мы ___ (ездить — to go by vehicle, ride, there and back or in general) гулять.
exercises.why: **ездим** is the present tense (1st person plural) of **ездить** (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **ехать** for one direction. present: я е́зжу · ты е́здишь · он е́здит · мы е́здим · вы е́здите · они е́здят. — Wiktionary, «ездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь).» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «По вечерам» marks a repeated or habitual action, which is the job of the many-directions verb.  Compare: «В прошлом году я ездил в Россию.» (I went to Russia (and returned) last year.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Да, я ходил (ездил) туда утром.» (Yes, I went there in the morning.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  From Александр Островский, «Бешеные деньги».
exercises.context: Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
